meta.description: Value-stress experiment: 5 sympy tasks × 3 policies testing value-aware observability and differential allocation
meta.note: First experiment with 3 policies. Uses stage_blind_tight as value-agnostic control. Primary test: do different policies resolve DIFFERENT task/value sets? Secondary: does BF beat BO on cost efficiency consistently?

policies.name: budget_only_tight
policies.description: Cost-only routing. No stage awareness, no tier escalation based on progress. Cap tight (0.50). Baseline for cost efficiency comparison.

policies.name: budgetflow_full_tight
policies.description: Full BudgetFlow with stage-aware weights (w_i = repair-heavy 1/3/2.5). Adaptive routing escalates to T3 when progress stalls.

policies.name: stage_blind_tight
policies.description: BudgetFlow with equal weights (w_i = 1/1/1). Still has adaptive routing and tier escalation, but no stage preference. Tests whether stage weighting adds value beyond basic adaptive routing.

tasks.reason: Easiest task in pool. Tests whether BF wastes T3 on already-easy tasks.
Very easy task. Both BO and BF resolved in 049 and 050 smokes.
Moderate-easy task. BF consistently cheaper than BO in prior smokes.
Mid-difficulty task. Anchor for historical difficulty scaling (1.0x).
Hardest task in easy pool (6.58x the easiest). Tests whether BF escalation helps on hard tasks.

design.estimated_cost: $1.50-$3.00 (based on prior smoke: ~$0.10-0.20 per task per policy)

H1_first_claim.description: Different policies resolve DIFFERENT task/value subsets. Specifically, bf_full solves harder (higher-value) tasks that bo and stage_blind miss.
H1_first_claim.test: Compare resolved sets across 3 policies. If sets differ, compute resolved_value and RVPD by policy. If bf_full has higher resolved_value (not just lower cost), First Claim gets independent evidence.
H1_first_claim.null_hypothesis: All 3 policies resolve the same tasks. RVPD differences are purely cost-driven.
H1_first_claim.evidence_required: At least one task resolved by bf_full but NOT by bo or stage_blind, AND that task must have non-trivial difficulty value.

H2_second_claim.description: BudgetFlow (both bf_full and stage_blind) is cheaper per task than budget_only.
H2_second_claim.test: Compare avg_cost, total_cost, turns, and RVPD across 3 policies.
H2_second_claim.null_hypothesis: BF is not cheaper than BO, or the savings are within noise.
H2_second_claim.evidence_required: BF policies show >= 15% cost reduction vs BO, consistent across tasks.

H3_stage_weight_ablation.description: bf_full (stage-aware weights) outperforms stage_blind (equal weights) on hard tasks.
H3_stage_weight_ablation.test: Compare bf_full vs stage_blind on hardest task (sympy-16988). Check if bf_full uses more T3 on REPAIR stage.
H3_stage_weight_ablation.null_hypothesis: Stage weights make no difference; bf_full == stage_blind on all metrics.
H3_stage_weight_ablation.evidence_required: bf_full shows distinct routing behavior (more T3 on REPAIR) and either better pass rate or lower cost on hard tasks.

claim_discipline.if_all_same_solved_set: Only Second Claim (cost efficiency) can be supported. First Claim remains 'observability validated; independent evidence pending.' Do NOT claim value allocation advantage.
claim_discipline.if_different_solved_sets: First Claim gets preliminary support. Report which tasks differ and whether the value spread is meaningful.
claim_discipline.if_bf_loses: Report honestly. Document whether the loss is cost-driven, pass-driven, or both. Do NOT spin.
